ogTitle: Lake Stevens Tile Installation With the Numbers Up Front
ogDesc: First big bathroom upgrade? Every Lake Stevens tile quote is itemized in writing, and every shower gets a bonded membrane plus a photographed 24-hour flood test before tile. Call (425) 595-1079.

roles.heroLead: Tile and grout let water through — the stopping is done by the membrane behind them. For a Lake Stevens family on its first big bathroom, that layer is the gap between a shower that outlasts the mortgage and a $40,000 framing repair. The order never changes: assembly, a 24-hour flood test with photos, then tile.
roles.costH2: How much does tile installation cost in Lake Stevens, WA?
roles.costP1: Straight numbers first: tile installation in Lake Stevens works out to $14–$26 per square foot, installed and all-in: tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor, with labor beginning at $11/sq ft. A standard tub-shower surround costs $3,200–$6,800. A bathroom done end to end, floor and shower and niche, generally totals $6,500 to $14,000.
roles.costP2: The line item that catches families off guard: format, not price tag, sets the labor. Small mosaic sheets mean more cuts and more grout lines, so a $4 sheet can genuinely cost more to install than $12 large-format porcelain. Budget by the layout, not the box.
roles.costNote: Installed August 2026 pricing for Lake Stevens — covering tile, labor and materials together. Trust the figure we put in writing at your free estimate; these bands just get you close.
roles.layersLead: Seven layers go under and around your tile, in order. Every shower failure we're brought into near Lake Stevens traces back to a skipped layer — the membrane most of the time — a few hundred dollars saved at build, five figures spent at repair.
roles.whyP1: What makes it expensive is the quiet start. Moisture slips the grout line, the substrate absorbs it, and the evidence arrives two years later as a soft spot in the hall or a mark on the ceiling below. That invoice covers framing, subfloor, drywall and a complete re-tile.
roles.whyP2: On a shower budget, waterproofing is roughly one dollar in ten. Deleting it is the single costliest choice a bathroom remodel can make.

roles.faqH2: Tile installation FAQ — Lake Stevens, WA
roles.faqQ1: How much does tile installation cost in Lake Stevens, WA?
roles.faqA1: The honest range for Lake Stevens: $14 to $26 per square foot installed, covering tile, setting materials, substrate prep and labor, with the labor portion starting at $11 per square foot. Tub-shower surrounds of standard size come to $3,200 to $6,800, and a complete bathroom — floor, shower, niche — usually finishes between $6,500 and $14,000. What swings the total most is format, not tile price: mosaic sheets and large-format tile each take considerably more labor per square foot than basic 12×12.
roles.faqQ2: How much does it cost to tile a shower in Lake Stevens?
roles.faqA2: For the standard alcove shower around Lake Stevens, the budget runs $3,200 up to $6,800, and your quote itemizes what's inside: demolition, bonded waterproofing, sloped pan or base, setting, niche, grout. Benches, curbless thresholds, steam and stone to the ceiling raise it — with the responsible line named on the quote each time. Waterproofing accounts for about one part in ten and is precisely what removes the tens-of-thousands failure from the table.
roles.faqQ3: Do you waterproof showers before tiling?
roles.faqA3: Yes, every shower, itemized on the quote so you can see it: pre-sloped base, a sheet or liquid membrane run up all four walls, sealing at corners, seams and pipe penetrations, and a 24-hour flood test documented with photos before any tile is set. We don't count cement board and thinset as waterproofing, because they aren't. Tile and grout pass water — the bonded membrane behind them is what protects the framing you paid for.
roles.faqQ4: How long does a bathroom tile job take?
roles.faqA4: Budget four to six working days for a Lake Stevens bathroom, and here's where they go: demolition and dust protection, then substrate and waterproofing with its 24-hour flood test, then one to two days of tile setting, then grout, silicone and trim. The grout wants 24 hours of cure before anyone showers. A floor by itself is usually a one-to-two-day job.
roles.faqQ5: Porcelain or ceramic tile — which is better?
roles.faqA5: Put the money where water and feet land. Denser than ceramic, chip-resistant, under 0.5% absorption — porcelain is the floor-and-shower material. Walls and backsplashes are ceramic territory, where its price advantage belongs. The Lake Stevens rule of thumb: every floor and every shower floor gets porcelain; walls are free to take ceramic or glass.
roles.faqQ6: Can you install a heated tile floor?
roles.faqA6: It can, and the math is friendly: figure $11 to $16 installed per square foot for an electric mat, thermostat inside that number. Know the catch going in — the upgrade only pays while the floor is already torn open, which is also what makes it the cheapest luxury a remodel can offer. Installation runs over an uncoupling membrane, with resistance readings taken before the setting bed and once more after the tile is down, and the mat claims a circuit of its own.
roles.faqQ7: Do I need to remove the old tile first?
roles.faqA7: Usually, and the cost is transparent: about $3.50 per square foot for removal and haul-away. That money buys the only real look at your subfloor — rot, movement, old leaks — and keeps the finished floor from sitting too high at doorways. Tiling over existing tile is an option only when the old floor is flat, solid and well bonded, and it hides exactly the problems we'd rather price at demo than discover after grout.
roles.faqQ8: How much does a kitchen backsplash cost in Lake Stevens?
roles.faqA8: A Lake Stevens kitchen backsplash costs $1,100 to $2,200 installed for the typical 30 square feet, outlet cuts, edge trim and color-matched grout included in the number. Where the top of the range comes from: mosaic sheets, herringbone, a picture-frame detail behind the stove, or slab-look porcelain run to the ceiling — the extra is layout and cutting time, and your quote breaks it out.
roles.faqQ9: Can you fix cracked tile or regrout instead of replacing?
roles.faqA9: Frequently — and it's the smaller bill, with repair and regrout opening at $8 per square foot. Right cases: grout that's stained or breaking down, a tile or two lost to impact, corners in the shower ready for silicone in place of grout. Wrong case: a substrate that's already done — hollow sounds underfoot, loosening that spreads, walls that move when pressed. Before writing either quote, we tell you plainly which bill your bathroom is actually facing.
roles.faqQ10: Which Lake Stevens neighborhoods do you tile?
roles.faqA10: All around the lake and beyond — Downtown Lake Stevens, North Cove, Frontier Village, Soper Hill, Cavelero Hill, Lundeen, Hartford, Sunnycrest, Glenwood and Hillcrest, plus Machias, Lochsloy, Lake Cassidy, Getchell, Three Lakes and Sisco Heights just outside town — and nearby Everett, Marysville, Snohomish, Granite Falls and the rest of Snohomish County.
roles.faqQ11: What warranty comes with tile installation?
roles.faqA11: Tile installation from OC Flooring comes with a 2-year workmanship warranty — twice our carpet coverage, because tile problems tend to show up in year two of ownership, not week two. Use a manufacturer's full waterproofing assembly and their system warranty applies alongside ours. Every membrane and flood test gets photographed, so you hold documentation, not just a promise, if the house ever goes on the market.
